title: Human Experts’ Evaluation of Generative AI for Contextualizing STEAM Education in the Global South
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether generative AI can improve the cultural responsiveness and pedagogical quality of STEAM lesson planning in Ghana. The central problem is that STEAM curricula in the Global South are often abstract, Western-centric, and poorly connected to learners’ local realities, languages, and cultural practices. The authors focus on lesson planning as a practical point where generative AI might help teachers localize instruction while still meeting curriculum standards.

The intervention evaluated is a customized Generative AI lesson-planning tool, the Culturally Responsive Lesson Planner (CRLP), powered by interactive semi-automated prompting. Four STEAM education experts independently reviewed paired lesson plans: standardized Ghana NaCCA lesson plans and CRLP-generated culturally responsive versions. They rated the plans with a 25-item rubric covering bias awareness, cultural representation, contextual relevance, linguistic responsiveness, and teacher agency, and also wrote qualitative reflections comparing the two lesson types. The content covered Mathematics, Science, Creative Arts and Design, and Computing at the basic and junior high levels in Ghana.

Findings suggest that CRLP-generated lessons were generally stronger than the NaCCA lessons in contextual relevance, teacher agency, and linguistic responsiveness. Experts valued the inclusion of indigenous knowledge, local artifacts, bilingual elements, and community-based examples that made the lessons more engaging and relevant. However, they also identified persistent weaknesses in cultural representation, translation accuracy, and the ability of GenAI to capture Ghana’s cultural pluralism without teacher mediation. The study concludes that GenAI can support culturally responsive STEAM planning, but only as a co-designer guided by human expertise, local knowledge, and careful checking for bias and cultural fit.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI lesson-planning assistant used to produce culturally responsive STEAM lesson plans through interactive prompting.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper evaluated a customized Culturally Responsive Lesson Planner (CRLP) powered by interactive semi-automated prompts to generate STEAM lesson plans, which were compared against NaCCA standards-based lesson plans.

findings.finding_summary: Four STEAM education experts (n=4) rated CRLP-generated lesson plans as stronger than NaCCA lesson plans on several culturally responsive dimensions, especially teacher agency (M=3.6) and contextual relevance (M=3.4). The GenAI-generated lessons were described as clearer, more student-centered, more engaging, and better connected to local community knowledge, although cultural representation remained the weakest domain (M=2.25) and translation accuracy was sometimes limited.
findings.measure: Validated 25-item Culturally Responsive Pedagogy Rubric and expert reflective comparisons across lesson plans

quality_tier_rationale: This is a convergent mixed-methods expert review with a very small purposive sample rather than an experimental impact study. The evidence is useful for comparative judgment but remains qualitative/mixed-methods and limited in generalizability.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports favorable expert ratings for GenAI-generated lesson plans, but no causal effect size on student outcomes or teacher performance is reported. The practical signal is positive, yet the magnitude of impact is unclear because the study measures rubric scores and reflections rather than direct instructional outcomes.
